Title: Smart team deployed to Nepal for humanitarian mission
Article:
SHAH ALAM: An 11-man team from Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) departed today to take part in a humanitarian mission in Nepal.
The rescue team left Subang Air Base aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft at about 9am, carrying various equipment, including communications gear.
The mission is led by Smart commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa, with the flight expected to take about five hours.

Title: German President calls for unity in democracy ahead of landmark vote
Article:
BONN, (Germany): German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on Friday called for the country's democracy and rule of law be protected from those "who scorn and trample all over them," ahead of Sunday's state election that can bring the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) to power.
"Ethnic-based thinking and nationalist isolationism are simply not the answer to the challenges of the 21st century," Steinmeier told a community festival attended by 2,000 volunteers at his secondary residence in Bonn, reported German news agency dpa.
Steinmeier, who steps down from office in March after ten years, described liberal democracy as an "achievement" and "a blessing for us all."
It helps to realise that those who wish to protect and preserve democracy represent the majority, said Steinmeier.
The comments came two days before the AfD is expected to win enough votes in the election in the eastern federal state of Saxony-Anhalt to take control there.
Founded in 2013, the rapidly ascendant party embraces a hard Euro-sceptic, anti-immigration platform steeped in far-right rhetoric, and is defiant of frequent calls for it to be banned from German political life as being outright extremist.
Anger and outrage offer no way forward, continued Steinmeier, who made no mention of the party or election in his comments. "You cannot build a future on hatred and incitement."
Addressing the volunteers gathered at the historic Villa Hammerschmidt, the 70-year-old president said: "We need people like you right now, and you all need the support of the many in our country — the large, often too silent majority." — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Pagoh bus rescue highlights Malaysian spirit [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A video showing Malaysians helping passengers escape an overturned express bus in Johor has won praise on social media, with many hailing it as a display of unity.
According to social media posts, the Singapore-bound bus reportedly lost control before overturning into a drain at Km120.9 of the southbound North-South Expressway between Pagoh and Yong Peng on Tuesday.
A video posted on Threads by user @kak_intannn, with the caption "Now this is the real 1Malaysia", has garnered more than 800,000 views and 36,000 likes.
The footage showed passengers helping one another evacuate after the bus' main door became inaccessible.
Some climbed out through the driver's door and a side emergency exit, while a man in a white shirt crouched down so passengers could step on his back to reach the ground.
Others waited below to support those climbing out, while another man inside the bus helped passengers through the opening.
Those at the scene were also heard offering to call an ambulance and checking whether everyone had evacuated.
The rescue effort drew widespread praise, with users describing it as a reflection of Malaysian unity and the spirit of helping one another.
"This is the Malaysia that we all love and want – one heart, one soul, helping one another and sharing every burden," Threads user @alyarazaliii wrote.
Another user, @atiqah_md_nooh, said her younger brother was involved in the accident and that everyone had escaped safely.
"Thank you to everyone who came forward and helped one another," she wrote.
The NST has contacted the authorities for further details on the accident.

Title: Serian records 376 API reading as of 8am
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Serian in Sarawak recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 376 as of 8am today.
The Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed the Serian district police headquarters station recorded the reading.
Three other areas in the state, namely Kuching, Samarahan and Sri Aman recorded very  unhealthy API readings at 273, 267 and 259 respectively.
As for unhealthy API, the areas in the state were Samalaju (191), Bintulu (190), ILP Miri (183), Mukah (183), Sarikei (179), Miri (176), Sibu (173), Limbang (156) and Kapit at 127.
Other stations recording unhealthy readings were Labuan (161), Batu Pahat (156), Kluang and Larkin (155), Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (155), Johan Setia (154), Bukit Rambai, Segamat and Pasir Gudang (153), Tangkak (152), Kota Tinggi (151), Kimanis (145), Romping (139), Balok Baru (118) and Kota Kinabalu (113)
A total of 30 stations recorded moderate API readings, while 10 recorded good readings.
API readings between 0 and 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are considered hazardous.
Yesterday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to the
declaration of an emergency
throughout Serian, Sarawak following worsening haze.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision was made after taking into consideration the advice of the prime minister and the Sarawak premier, as well as relevant agencies, regarding air quality levels in the affected area.

Title: US midterms begin with chaos over mail-voting crackdown
Article:
WASHINGTON: America's midterm elections opened Friday in a fog of confusion over mail voting, with ballots already going out as President Donald Trump presses courts to let him impose sweeping new restrictions on how they are handled.
North Carolina became the first state authorised to begin sending out ballots, formally launching an election season that culminates on November 3 and will determine control of Congress for the final two years of Trump's term.
Yet voters and election officials still do not know what rules may govern millions of mail ballots, as Trump asks the Supreme Court to revive curbs blocked by a federal judge and as states scramble to prepare for changes that could come after voting has begun.
The dispute has been compounded by whistleblower allegations that a new Postal Service verification system was rushed, inadequately tested and could delay or even disqualify entire batches of ballots because of a single barcode problem.
A federal judge on Friday extended her previous temporary block on Trump's plan, a day after warning that hurried changes could cause widespread disruption.
"We're not playing an intellectual puzzle game," Judge Indira Talwani reportedly told a lawyer defending the restrictions, in remarks widely picked up by US media. "We're talking about people's right to vote."
The Trump administration is expected to appeal to the Supreme Court against Talwani's new order, which extends her previous block.
Rules in limbo
Trump's March executive order would require states to provide the US Postal Service with lists of eligible mail voters through a new federal portal.
Ballot envelopes would also need individual barcodes and other design features, with USPS empowered to refuse mailings that fail to meet its requirements.
The administration says the rules are meant to protect election integrity, although it has produced no evidence of significant fraud through mail voting.
Trump has repeatedly denounced the practice as corrupt while using it himself – including to vote in Florida's Republican primary just last month.
The uncertainty comes on top of a voting system that already differs dramatically from state to state.
Some automatically send ballots to registered voters, others require voters to request them, while identification requirements, return deadlines and rules for counting late-arriving ballots vary across the country.
Election officials now face the additional prospect of federal requirements changing while voting is already underway.
"The states set the time, place and manner of elections in this country, not the president," Marc Elias, the founder of voting rights platform Democracy Docket, said on his YouTube show.
"In fact, the Congress can override the states in many instances, but in no instance can the president. The president is given no power over federal elections."
North Carolina officials said Friday's mailings would proceed normally and that the state has no plans to use the federal portal at the centre of the dispute.
But time is rapidly running out for any nationwide overhaul.
'Rushed, chaotic'
Friday marks 60 days before Election Day – the deadline Trump's order itself envisioned for states to submit voter information – while another 18 states are expected to begin distributing ballots roughly 45 days before Nov 3.
That leaves little room for officials to redesign envelopes, update computer systems, train workers and upload voter data if the courts suddenly allow the restrictions to take effect.
Concerns intensified this week after an anonymous USPS whistleblower alleged that the ballot portal had been developed through a "rushed, chaotic, and fundamentally flawed" process.
The official warned that under a proposed "zero-per-cent failure" policy, one barcode that fails to scan or match could result in an entire batch containing thousands of ballots being rejected until it is checked again.
USPS told AFP no mandatory verification procedures were being performed and that election officials would initially use its portal only voluntarily.
The fight – alongside disputes over partisan redistricting in around a dozen states – comes with high political stakes.
Republicans hold narrow congressional majorities, but Democrats are favoured to capture the House as Trump's approval ratings remain weak and voters voice frustration over living costs and the continuing war with Iran.
A new Cornell University forecast gives Democrats an eight-in-10 chance of taking the chamber, projecting a roughly 226-209 majority.

Title: Malaysians grateful for  help at critical moment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  The sound of firecrackers during Ramadan is no longer just a familiar festive noise for Malaysian evacuee Muhammad Tarmimi Tarmizi, but a reminder of the missile attack he experienced in Qatar.
For the 49-year-old logistics coordinator, it is a sound that takes him back to Qatar, where missile debris fell just 10km from where he was, turning an ordinary day into a frightening race to safety.
"Whenever I hear a sound similar to a bomb, I would immediately jump and become startled.
"For a moment, my mind would take me back to what happened in Qatar," he told the
New Straits Times.
He is among the 163 Malaysians brought home by the government.
Tarmimi, who had been in Doha, Qatar for almost a month, was at a shopping mall with a colleague when the missiles fell.
Immediately after the attack, he and his colleague were evacuated from the Qatari capital in a  23-hour bus journey  to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
Tarmimi said the uncertainty over whether airports would remain open and routes would remain safe was more exhausting than the physical journey itself.
Relief came when they reached Jeddah Airport, where Malaysian authorities had arranged an evacuation flight home.
For Malaysian student Hanees Shafe, an umrah  similarly turned into  anxious uncertainty when conflict erupted in the Middle East and the Malaysian Embassy in Saudi Arabia offered her a flight home.
She said she initially thought reports of the Iran-United States war circulating in her WhatsApp groups were no different from previous conflicts in the region.
[[nid:1526021]]
"After spending a week in Madinah, news began circulating in our WhatsApp group about the Iran-US war. I thought it was just another ordinary conflict that happens from time to time."
Although she was relieved that Makkah and Madinah were not affected by the missile attacks, Hanees said she could not shake off the fear of being stranded in Saudi Arabia.
She eventually returned to Madinah before accepting a flight offered by the Malaysian embassy as part of efforts to bring Malaysians home.
Hanees said Malaysian Embassy officials treated the evacuees "like family" throughout the journey, from the moment they arrived at Jeddah Airport until they reached Malaysia.
"When we arrived at Jeddah Airport, they came to pick us up and brought us to the haj and umrah terminal."
It was only while she was on her way to the Madinah train station that Hanees realised just how crucial the embassy's intervention had been.
"I received an email saying my flight  to Istanbul on March 23 had been cancelled.
"I felt safe knowing I had made the right decision to accept the ticket offered by the embassy," she said.
She was among 163 Malaysians evacuated from the conflict zone who arrived safely at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on March 11.
The Foreign Ministry said it would continue monitoring developments in the Middle East and support coordination efforts led by the National Security Council to safeguard the safety and welfare of Malaysians.

Title: Freedom Flotilla announces new mission to Gaza in October
Article:
ISTANBUL: The Freedom Flotilla Coalition announced a new international maritime mission to the Gaza Strip, with vessels making stops at European ports before a planned attempt to reach the enclave in October, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.
"We are sailing again because Israel hasn't stopped its genocide and because Palestine is still not free," the coalition said in an appeal for international sup
port.
The mission seeks to challenge Israel's blockade of Gaza and mobilise public pressure across Europe, the coalition said in a statement published Wednesday.
The voyage is already underway, with the coalition's Handala II vessel having visited ports in Norway, Sweden and Denmark during June and July.
Another vessel, the Kate, departed from the British city of Bristol in August and subsequently made stops in Ireland, Germany and France, according to the statement.
The vessels are expected to visit ports in Spain, Portugal and Italy before continuing toward Gaza, where the coalition plans to arrive in October.
The mission brings together human rights advocates, trade union activists, elected representatives, journalists, medical professionals and other supporters of Palestinian rights, the coalition said.
The coalition said it would work with local communities to pressure governments to block weapons and energy shipments to Israel, end diplomatic and military cooperation with it and impose sanctions.
"The Freedom Flotilla sails again because our governments continue to fail to uphold their obligations," said Zohar Chamberlain Regev, a member of the coalition's steering committee.
"At every port, we will carry the demand that Palestinians be free to live with dignity.
"In October, we intend to carry that demand and the solidarity of people around the world to Gaza's shores," she added.
The coalition urged governments to demand safe and unobstructed passage for the flotilla and to make clear that any attack, seizure or detention of its participants would have consequences.
It also called for immediate and unrestricted access to Gaza and an end to Israeli restrictions on the entry of food, water, medicine and other essential supplies.
Governments should defend freedom of navigation and use diplomatic, economic and legal measures to end the blockade, it added.
"We know that sailing toward Gaza carries serious risks.
"But silence and inaction carry a much greater cost for Palestinians and the world," he said, describing the mission as "an expression of shared humanity and a refusal to accept the destruction of an entire people as normal," said Edward Digilio, an engineer from the US state of Maryland participating in the initiative.
The coalition said Israeli forces had attacked and detained hundreds of flotilla participants during an earlier mission in the spring of 2026.
It said volunteers reported severe beatings, broken bones, gunshot wounds, repeated tasering and sexual assault while in Israeli custody.
It also recalled Israel's May 2010 raid on the Gaza-bound Mavi Marmara, during which 10 activists were killed. — BERNAMAS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mexican ruling-party lawmaker found dead with gunshot wound, a year before elections
Article:
MEXICO CITY: A member of Congress from Mexico's ruling Morena party was found dead from a gunshot wound in the eastern state of Veracruz on Friday, less than a year before local and federal elections.
Zenyazen Escobar, a federal legislator representing the coastal state — home to some of the country's oil complexes — was found dead inside his car with at least one gunshot wound.
"The investigation file is being compiled," state Attorney General Lisbeth Jimenez told reporters, without providing further details.
The secretary-general of Veracruz, Ricardo Ahued, said the lawmaker's vehicle showed no signs of violence.
Mexico's lower house of Congress expressed its condolences to Escobar's family and friends and urged judicial authorities to conduct a "thorough investigation into the facts".
The death occurred as the country prepares to hold elections on June 6 to renew mayoral, state legislative, city council and gubernatorial positions.
In previous elections, various regions have experienced incidents of violence linked to organised crime groups seeking to co-opt political figures and consolidate territorial control.
According to the human rights organisation Data Civica, in July alone there were at least 30 incidents of "political-criminal violence" across 11 states in Mexico, 14 of which were homicides.
The states with the highest registered cases were Zacatecas, with 10 cases; Michoacan and Quintana Roo, with four each; Oaxaca, with three; and Baja California and Veracruz, with two each.
Data Civica describes political-criminal violence as threats, murders, armed attacks, assassination attempts, disappearances and kidnappings.
The national electoral body INE has warned that organised crime represents one of the most serious concerns for democratic processes.
According to the INE, court rulings have in the past documented the presence of armed individuals seeking to intimidate or coerce the public into voting a certain way, as well as acts of theft and the burning of election materials.

Title: Tetris distances itself from controversial White House 'arcade' games
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: Tetris said on Friday that it did not give permission for the White House to use the game's iconic imagery for a controversial online arcade that the Trump administration released on Thursday.
"The Tetris Company was not involved in the creation of 'Build the Wall' and did not authorise or license the Tetris brand or intellectual property for the game," Tetris told AFP in a statement.
"We are currently reviewing the matter," the statement continued.
A block-stacking game called Build the Wall included instructions to "protect the border from the coming horde".
The arcade-style games and promotional content used by the Trump administration contain images that resemble games created by Tetris and other major game developers, including Sega, Microsoft-owned Xbox and the Flappy Bird Foundation.
"At Tetris, we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them," Tetris said in a social media post.
"P.P.S. We take copyright infringement very seriously," the post continued.
Promotional content posted by the White House on social media also included images that resemble trademarks and designs from Microsoft-owned Xbox.
Microsoft did not respond to requests for comment, and Sega Corporation could not immediately be reached.
The White House released several games Thursday, with a placeholder that teased another one "coming soon".
The web-only games, which were published on the official White House website under a new page called "arcade", sparked condemnation for racist themes and prompted questions about potential copyright violations.
In one clip, the letters from the Sega logo transform into MAGA, a term that stands for Make America Great Again, which President Trump turned into his campaign slogan during his first presidential run for the 2016 election.
A game called "Flappy Bill" features a bald eagle carrying a document in its claws that tries to avoid smashing into columns of various heights, against a background that resembles Washington DC.
"This administration is laser focused on ways to innovate and tell the story of the President's many accomplishments in a way that resonates with every American," the White House said Thursday in a statement to AFP.
Rights groups criticised the White House.
"Makes me sick. They've been playing games with people's lives for years, now they've made a video game of what they're doing," Amerika Garcia Grewal, co-director of the Frontera Federation in Eagle Pass, Texas, told AFP.
"There's no attention paid to the quality of life for human beings, both those in their game or those in real life. We who live in the borderlands are US citizens and yet are treated with suspicion and violence," she added.
The game designers "have lost touch with what it means to be human and care for others".
Trump campaigned on a promise to expel millions of undocumented migrants and has taken several actions since returning to power aimed at speeding up deportations and reducing border crossings.
His White House meanwhile has long used social media stunts to ram home its points and troll liberal opponents, and has sparked a backlash from several artists by using their music without permission.
The White House is trying to convince voters that Trump's second presidential term has been successful ahead of the midterm election in November. The balance of power in Congress will also be at stake when Americans go to the polls in just over two months.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: The new arms race is moving into space
Article:
In June, a secretive unmanned Chinese spaceplane closely monitored by United States military analysts released a small satellite hundreds of miles above Earth in an orbital region crowded with commercial and military satellites.
The object then looped around another Chinese satellite before returning towards the spaceplane, according to US space-tracking firm LeoLabs.
The US military operates a similarly secretive spaceplane resembling a small shuttle, also with no crew.
Both programmes reflect the rapidly evolving field of military space operations as Beijing and Washington prepare for the possibility of conflict extending into space.
Chinese researchers linked to the military are developing technologies ranging from satellites designed to pursue and even capture other spacecraft to systems that could extend fuel supplies while doing so, according to a  review of patent-related documents, procurement notices and academic papers.
And the US and Britain conducted their first joint military operation in space in the path of a suspected Chinese spy satellite, according to commercial space-tracking data.
"The Chinese are rapidly developing capabilities", including ground- and space-based weapons designed to interfere with or destroy targets, US Space Force's chief of space operations General Chance Saltzman said in July.
The threat from China is "substantial", added Saltzman, who is retiring.
Satellites have become indispensable to modern warfare,
as conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East have demonstrated.
For decades they have provided communications, navigation and intelligence services to armed forces on Earth, and once placed in orbit typically remained on fixed paths.
Increasingly, militaries view them as active weapons platforms capable of launching attacks by disrupting a satellite's operations through jamming or laser dazzling, or even capturing enemy spacecraft.
Disruption of US space capabilities would "cripple our massive military in the terrestrial sphere", affecting everything from surveillance to missile defence, said Everett Dolman, a former professor at the US Air Force's Air War College.
Spaceplanes, because they are agile and capable of deploying satellites or carrying cargo, could appear to opponents as potential "space fighters", he said.
SpaceX, which recently debuted on public markets, operates about 11,000 Starlink satellites and plans a constellation of larger artificial intelligence-enabled data centres in space.
China is building rival networks, while US President Donald Trump's Golden Dome missile defence programme envisions space-based interceptors.
The US is also refining capabilities that could prove important in a future conflict.
In the joint US-British operation in September last year, US space forces working from a base in Colorado directed a US military satellite to swoop in close to a United Kingdom one as China's Shiyan 12-01 satellite passed about 83 kilometres beneath them, according to space intelligence company Slingshot Aerospace.
Three space experts with military backgrounds told Reuters it appeared intended as a signal to Beijing, including at space-tracking firm COMSPOC.
Andrew Turner, a retired senior British air force officer who is now a space consultant, said it was "almost certainly a strategic signal to China" to demonstrate allied unity, capability and a warning to not interfere with the UK satellite.
The US and Britain publicly announced the operation, the first known one between two members of the "Five Eyes" intelligence alliance, but did not disclose its proximity to a Chinese spacecraft.
Much of what occurs in space remains classified because of its intelligence implications.
China's Foreign Ministry said it was not familiar with the specific details of the US-British operation.
More broadly, Beijing opposes the weaponisation of space and supports its peaceful use, the ministry said, while accusing Washington of stoking an arms race through efforts including the missile defence system Golden Dome and potential space-based weapons.
Asked about Shiyan 12-01, state news agency Xinhua has described Shiyan 12-01 as conducting space environment surveys, and the spaceplane as an experimental craft supporting the peaceful use of space.
US Space Command head General Stephen Whiting has repeatedly emphasised the importance of space to modern warfare, warning that adversaries are developing capabilities to deny the US access to key systems and reduce military effectiveness.
He has said adversaries would likely seek to target US space assets early in a conflict.
"We must be well-prepared for conflict in space. And if deterrence fails, we will fight and win," he told a conference in April.
The writers are from Reuters

Title: Panama Canal begins reducing crossings due to El Nino
Article:
PANAMA CITY: The Panama Canal on Friday began reducing the number of ships passing through due to a drought caused by the El Nino weather phenomenon.
The Panama Canal Authority said low water levels in the two artificial lakes that feed the canal forced it to act.
The number of vessels allowed through the waterway connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans will be progressively lowered from 36 per day to 32 by mid-September.
Panama has declared a nationwide emergency over El Nino, a weather pattern developing over the Pacific Ocean that is triggering worldwide changes in winds, atmospheric pressure and rainfall and pushing up global temperatures.
This year's El Nino is expected to be the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago.
It has not yet reached its peak, but Central America is already in the throes of a severe drought, prompting Honduras and El Salvador to also declare emergencies.
The Panama Canal handles five per cent of global maritime trade and around 40 per cent of US container traffic.
It has already implemented other water conservation measures, such as lowering the maximum draft – the vessel's depth in the water – for the largest ships.
In 2023, El Nino forced the canal authority to reduce the number of daily crossings to 22 vessels.

Title: UN adopts new map with smaller US, bigger Africa
Article:
UNITED NATIONS: The United Nations General Assembly voted Friday to adopt a new world map that makes the African continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe, drawing ire from Washington.
Aimed at "a more accurate representation" of continental landmasses, the resolution was supported by 164 countries, while the US voted against it and six other states abstained.
The new map – known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection – improves "the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world", the resolution said.
It urges member states to use the new map in place of the traditional Mercator projection, which was designed for maritime navigation by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569.
Foreign Minister Robert Dussey of Togo, which sponsored the resolution, said maps "guide education, nourish the imagination, and influence collective perceptions."
"They are therefore never neutral; when they present a distorted image of our planet, they risk perpetuating inaccurate representation that is passed down through generations."
The US, however, slammed the resolution, saying such moves are "the reason this institution is losing its credibility".
"Instead of focusing on genuine problems... this body is debating map projects from the 16th century and their role in promoting reparations and cognitive justice," US representative Yaryna Ferencevych said ahead of the vote.
'Distorted representation'
The Mercator projection focused on accurate depictions of the shapes and angles of land masses, but their relative sizes were often inaccurate – largely due to the challenge of rendering a three-dimensional globe onto a two-dimensional map.
It inflated northern regions and compressed equatorial ones, making Europe and North America appear much larger, while shrinking Africa and South America.
A group of cartographers launched the Equal Earth projection in 2018. It makes Africa, Latin America, South Asia and Oceania appear much larger.
"Equal Earth preserves the relative surface areas of continents and, as much as possible, shows their shapes as they appear on a globe," one of the cartographers, Bojan Savric, told AFP in 2025.
France – which co-sponsored the resolution in support of the new map – announced Friday that it would abandon the Mercator projection.
In that map, "the United States, Russia and China take on a disproportionate visual prominence compared to Africa, Latin America or southeast Asia", while "Greenland appears almost as big as Africa", Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said.
"Changing maps obviously doesn't change the world," he said. "But correcting a distorted representation is already an act of truth."
The initiative comes as France is seeking to improve relations with Africa, particularly in former colonies with which it has prickly ties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UniMAP accelerates AI, semiconductor research
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) is stepping up its artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor research drive to turn academic breakthroughs into practical solutions that strengthen Malaysia's industrial competitiveness.
UniMAP vice-chancellor Datuk Professor Dr Zaliman Sauli said the university is committed to ensuring its research delivers tangible solutions to real-world challenges.
He said this included strengthening industry partnerships, expanding international networks and intensifying applied research in sustainable energy, green manufacturing, digital transformation and advanced technologies.
Zaliman said this in his speech at the Global Trends in Engineering, Science & Technology Congress 2026 (GTEST 2026) at the Penang Waterfront Convention Centre here on Tuesday.
Zaliman said GTEST 2026 reflected UniMAP's efforts to bridge the gap between research and impact.
He added that the congress theme, "Advancing Sustainable Futures Through Global Solutions", aligned with UniMAP's mission to develop sustainable and high-impact solutions while preparing graduates for a rapidly changing world.
Universiti Malaysia Perlis chancellor Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizzuddin Putra Jamalullail (seventh from left) overseeing the exchange of memoranda of understanding and memoranda of agreement during the Global Trends in Engineering, Science & Technology Congress 2026 at the Penang Waterfront Convention Centre on Tuesday. NSTP PIC BY AURIS FAQRURAZZI
"The future belongs to those who can look beyond disciplinary boundaries and imagine new possibilities through collaboration and creativity," he said.
"Our graduates must not only be job seekers but also job creators."
GTEST 2026 attracted about 500 research papers for presentation across 11 conferences, alongside a product pitching session, creating a multidisciplinary platform for researchers, academics and industry players.
It covers electrical engineering, robotics and intelligent systems, civil and environmental engineering, chemical and materials engineering, sustainable energy, green materials, applied engineering and technology, innovation and business matching, global communication and linguistics, and medical engineering research.
UniMAP chancellor Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizzuddin Putra Jamalullail said research must go beyond publications and be translated into practical applications capable of improving human well-being and protecting the environment.
"While the world continues to explore new frontiers in science and technology, progress and sustainability must move hand in hand," he said when opening the congress.
He added that GTEST 2026 provided an important platform for researchers, academics, industry leaders and policymakers from around the world to exchange knowledge, expertise and ideas.
The congress also marked UniMAP's silver jubilee, commemorating 25 years of the university's contribution to education, research and development.
In a further push to strengthen industry links, UniMAP exchanged memoranda of understanding with Renesas Semiconductor Malaysia Sdn Bhd, Aemulus Corporation Sdn Bhd, Toyo Tyre Malaysia Sdn Bhd, AT&S Austria Technologie & Systemtechnik (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, Altera Malaysia and other partners.
Memoranda of agreement were also exchanged with Cancer Survivors Malaysia, Renesas Electronics (Penang) Sdn Bhd and ADA Biotech Sdn Bhd.
The collaborations are expected to expand opportunities in research, innovation and talent development, reinforcing UniMAP's role in connecting academia, industry and global research networks.

Title: Reclaiming our future from corruption
Article:
LETTERS:
I fully agree with the important message in Sharanjit Singh's NST article — it is truly time to put an end to corruption that takes so much from our country.
The report shows that over 26 years, we have lost an estimated RM4.5 trillion.
This is not just a number — it is a loss felt by every Malaysian. It takes away from what we have today, and limits what we can build for our future.
We are seeing more cases brought before the courts than ever before.
People from all levels — public officials, civil servants, and business leaders with titles — are being charged across both government and private sector establishments.
Problems once kept hidden are now coming to light. It is a sad development  of our times that wrongdoing has become so widespread, and seems so common, blatant and shameless.
What matters most is not just the money lost. It is the trust that is being damaged — trust in our institutions, trust in our leaders, and belief that our society is fair.
When people in power misuse their position for personal benefit, ordinary citizens lose faith.
Resources meant for schools, hospitals, public works, and those in need are diverted elsewhere — leaving our nation poorer and less united.
As the article notes, corruption appears everywhere — in finance, government, business, and even our natural resources. But we are also reminded that looking the other only allows it to continue.
The fact that cases are now being heard in court is a hopeful sign that our system is working — yet justice must be fair, consistent, and applied equally to all.
This is not only a matter for the authorities. It concerns every one of us. We should expect honesty, openness, and responsibility from those who serve us.
In this way, we can begin to recover what was lost, rebuild public trust, and ensure our nation's wealth is used for the good of all Malaysians — not for the benefit of a few.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Kuala Lumpur

Title: NST Leader: Gaza cannot be emptied in plain sight
Article:
IF anyone had an iota of doubt in 1947 that the Zionists would one day drive out the Palestinians from Gaza, it is now crystal clear that was the strategy all along.

Title: Najib, Rosmah legal wins, custody deaths and Shah Alam murder charges among key court cases this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It was a week of significant legal victories for members of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's family, while the country's highest court paved the way for important questions on deaths in custody to be examined.
Najib, his wife Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor and their son Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin each secured favourable rulings in separate proceedings.
The former prime minister and Nazifuddin obtained a stay of bankruptcy proceedings over RM1.7 billion in unpaid taxes while Rosmah succeeded in her bid to introduce fresh evidence in her solar hybrid corruption appeal.
Meanwhile, the Federal Court agreed to hear appeals involving two deaths in custody, while eight men were charged with the murder of a 23-year-old man during a brawl in Shah Alam.
The week also saw an army veteran carrying a "Datuk" title charged in Melaka with outraging the modesty of a young golf caddy, while the Sessions Court rejected a DNAA bid by Maju Holdings executive chairman Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife in their criminal breach of trust and money-laundering case.
Below are some of the major court cases this week:
Rosmah allowed to introduce fresh evidence in solar graft appeal
Rosmah began the week with a major breakthrough in her appeal against her conviction in the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid corruption case.
The Court of Appeal unanimously allowed her application to introduce fresh evidence involving prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, who was a consultant for Jepak Holdings Sdn Bhd.
The fresh evidence includes allegations by Rayyan that his testimony had been given under pressure.
Rayyan had testified during the trial that he witnessed two black bags purportedly containing RM1.5 million being delivered to Rosmah's Langgak Duta residence in September 2017.
Najib, son win stay against RM1.7 billion bankruptcy proceedings
Najib and his son Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin scored a legal victory at the Court of Appeal on Friday when they succeeded in staying bankruptcy proceedings brought against them by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
A three-member bench held there were specific issues raised by Najib and Nazifuddin that had to be determined by the Special Commissioners of Income Tax (SCIT), constituting sufficient grounds for a stay.
The tax authority is seeking RM1.69 billion from Najib and RM37.6 million from Nazifuddin.
The stay will remain pending the disposal of their appeals before the SCIT against the additional tax assessments.
Apex court to hear appeals over deaths in custody
Two deaths in custody cases will now receive scrutiny from the Federal Court involving gravedigger Mohd Fadzrin Zaidi and security guard M. Thinagaran.
A three-member bench comprising Datuk Nordin Hassan, Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and Datuk Azmi Ariffin allowed the appeals on questions concerning the duty of care owed to detainees.
One question is whether the nature of an offence allegedly committed by a detainee should be considered when determining whether suicide was reasonably foreseeable.
Mohd Fadzrin, 29, was found hanged at the Seberang Perai Utara police headquarters lock-up in 2019, a day after he was arrested during a drug raid.
In the separate case, Thinagaran, 31, was found dead while detained at a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency lock-up in Klang in 2019.
His family had succeeded in a negligence suit at the High Court, but that decision was subsequently overturned by the Court of Appeal, prompting them to turn to the Federal Court.
Eight charged with killing man in Shah Alam brawl
Eight men, including two brothers, were charged this week over the death of a man following a brawl in Shah Alam.
The group was brought before court to face a charge of killing the victim during the altercation.
The case was among the week's more serious violent-crime prosecutions, involving multiple accused persons arising from the same incident.
No plea was recorded as the murder charge falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Army veteran charged with outraging modest of caddy
In Melaka, an army veteran with a "Datuk" title was charged with outraging the modesty of a 20-year-old female golf caddy.
Yahya Hashim, 68, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Uthman Abd Ghani at the Ayer Keroh Magistrate's Court.
The alleged incident took place last month and involved the young woman while she was working as a golf caddy.
Yahya claimed trial to the charge.
Abu Sahid, wife fail in DNAA bid
The Sessions Court on Friday rejected a bid by Maju Holdings executive chairman Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife Puan Sri Noor Azrina Mohd Azmi for a Discharge Not Amounting to an Acquittal (DNAA) in their CBT and money-laundering case.
Their lawyer Datuk Jasbeer Singh sought the discharge on grounds that the prosecution had yet to provide several key documents almost a year after the couple were charged.
Abu Sahid faces CBT charges involving RM313 million and money-laundering charges involving RM139 million linked to the proposed MEX II highway project.
Noor Azrina, meanwhile, is accused of receiving RM67.14 million in proceeds from unlawful activities into her bank account between March and November 2017.

Title: Trump says Iran war is 'small potatoes' for US
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said Friday that the Iran war was "small potatoes" for the US, in his administration's latest bid to play down the conflict ahead of crucial midterm elections.
Trump's comments came a day after Vice President JD Vance said that "I wouldn't call it a war" despite an upsurge in clashes between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz.
"A lot of people don't call it a war. I call it a military conflict because it's small potatoes for us," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked about Vance's remarks.
"It's not a big thing. We did Venezuela, and we did this," added Trump, who was surrounded by cattle ranchers invited for the signing of two executive orders on beef processing.
The six-month-old war in which 18 US troops and thousands of Iranians have died has reached a stalemate, with Tehran disrupting shipping traffic in the strategic waterway.
But with fuel prices threatening to cost Trump's Republicans their control of Congress in November's midterms, his administration has been trying to minimise the conflict.
Trump said the US was carrying out "intermittent strikes" but that "we're not fighting right now."
He reiterated his claims that the US effectively controlled the Strait of Hormuz and had decimated Iran's military.
"What we've done is amazing. We took over Venezuela and we have essentially taken over Iran," Trump said.
Pressed on calling the war "small potatoes" when 18 service members died, an increasingly irate Trump compared the Iran war to the years-long US wars in Vietnam and Afghanistan.
"I don't think it matters what you call it. What matters is the fact we have had tremendous success. We've stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon," he said.

Title: Penang shooting, airport cannabis haul and RM260m oil seizure among key crime cases this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A manhunt is underway for two men who shot and injured a 43-year-old mechanic at a car workshop in Jalan Sungai Lembu, Bukit Mertajam, Penang on Aug 3.
The victim sustained a gunshot wound to his right palm after the suspects, who were riding a motorcycle, approached him and opened fire.
The victim ran about 50 metres from the workshop before jumping over a fence opposite a Chinese cemetery to escape.
Police and forensic personnel later found bullets and spent cartridges at the scene, while investigations are ongoing to establish the motive.
Police also found that the victim has a previous criminal record.
Below are some of the major crimes reported in the country this week.
Gaps in security screening at the country's airports have come under scrutiny again after a Malaysian man boarded a flight carrying 3.452kg of hydroponic cannabis before Indian authorities arrested him in Chennai.
The 62-year-old was arrested by Indian Customs at Chennai International Airport on Aug 31 after arriving from Kuala Lumpur, with the drugs worth about RM520,000 allegedly concealed in a false-bottom compartment in his checked-in baggage.
The case is the second involving a Malaysian allegedly carrying hydroponic cannabis into Chennai within a month, after Indian Customs arrested a 54-year-old Malaysian from Perak with 4.033kg of the drug on Aug 8 after he arrived from Bangkok.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail later acknowledged that gaps remained in Malaysia's outbound and inbound security systems, particularly at airports, and said the government was taking steps to strengthen checks.
In Putrajaya, a 30-year-old cook was arrested after five police reports were lodged against him for allegedly causing a commotion and provoking the public during the National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31.
It was reported that the suspect surrendered on Aug 2 and later tested positive for tetrahydrocannabinol (THC).
Police are now awaiting further instructions from the Deputy Public Prosecutor's office.
Seven witnesses were called in to assist investigations into the incident, which stemmed from a dispute over seating on the day.
In Johor, the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) seized two ships and an oil cargo worth an estimated RM260 million following a suspected illegal ship-to-ship transfer in Tanjung Buai waters on Sep 1.
MMEA Tanjung Sedili Zone acting director Maritime Commander Mohd Najib Sam said the vessels, a Malaysian-registered tugboat and dredger, were detained at 3.20am after being spotted alongside each other about 1.4 nautical miles northwest of Tanjung Buai.
He said the tugboat had five crew members, comprising Malaysians and Indonesians aged between 26 and 58, while the dredger had 13 Malaysian crew members aged between 22 and 51. Both vessels and the oil cargo were detained for further investigation.
The case was being investigated under Section 491B(1)(K) and (L) of the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952 for allegedly conducting ship-to-ship activities and anchoring without approval, as well as under the Customs Act 1967 over the undocumented oil cargo.

Title: Opponents seek to block US from starting work on Trump arch in Washington
Article:
WASHINGTON: A group of three military veterans and an architectural historian on Friday asked a US judge to block the Trump administration from starting work on a triumphal arch in Washington.
The US Interior Department on Thursday announced plans to move forward soon with work for the 250-foot (76-metre) arch near Arlington National Cemetery despite legal challenges and the lack of final approval from a government planning authority.
In a US District Court filing on Friday seeking a temporary restraining order, lawyers for the plaintiffs said the administration has "no legal basis for the construction work". They said the arch violates federal law and needs approval from Congress.
The administration has argued a 1925 law that authorised a now-defunct commission to build Washington's Arlington Memorial Bridge provides congressional approval for the arch, which the opponents dispute.
Despite Thursday's announcement on X by Interior Secretary Doug Burgum of work starting after "a very long wait", the government said in a court filing Friday the planned excavation work at the arch site was "not construction, or demolition in preparation for construction, of an arch".
The government added in its court filing that it plans to dig four "test pits" to assess if any artefacts or cultural materials are present, starting on or after Sept 21. It said it would restore the site by Oct 31.
The arch is part of Trump's broader effort to leave his architectural mark on America's capital city, with projects including a new White House ballroom, renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and redevelopment of a golf course in East Potomac Park.
With a design evoking Paris' Arc de Triomphe, the monument would rise near Arlington National Cemetery, a military burial ground, which supporters say would honour the sacrifice of American veterans.
Opponents say the arch would destroy the cemetery's carefully designed historic sight line between Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House.
The project also has yet to receive final approval from the National Capital Planning Commission, which is considering whether to grant an exception to the 130-foot (40-metre) building height limit that applies to most of Washington.
US District Judge Tanya Chutkan in April sharply questioned Trump's authority to build the arch. The government in April agreed to provide 14 days' notice before starting construction.
The Interior Department reiterated that notice plan on Friday.
In the Friday court filing, opponents of the project pointed to Trump's construction of a ballroom on the White House grounds as a "cautionary tale", saying the government proceeded with construction even though a District Court found it unlawful and the Circuit Court affirmed the ruling.
The US Supreme Court last week in a 5-4 ruling let ballroom construction continue while Trump challenges a judicial order that would halt much of the development, with Chief Justice John Roberts in a dissent calling the project "likely unlawful".

Title: US sinks third alleged Ecuador drug gang boat in a week
Article:
QUITO: The US military said it had blown up another boat with alleged links to Ecuadoran drug gangs, bringing to three the number of vessels it has sunk in the area in a week.
Thursday's operation by US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) is part of a broader US campaign of strikes on alleged Latin American drug boats that have left more than 200 people dead since last year.
Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said on X it struck a vessel "operating as a floating refuelling station in support of illicit at-sea drug trafficking operations" in the Eastern Pacific.
It said its intelligence had confirmed the vessel was working with Los Choneros, a "violent narco-terrorist organisation". This is a notorious Ecuadoran gang that has ties to Mexico's Sinaloa cartel.
Crew members safe
It added that an unspecified number of individuals aboard the boat had been "safely transferred" to authorities in Ecuador before the sinking, which came a day after a separate US strike.
Ecuador's Navy said it received 28 crew members from that vessel and the boat that was sunk on Wednesday.
On Friday last week, the military also destroyed a boat after intercepting and evacuating the crew.
In Manta, the country's main fishing port, a group of people awaited news Friday of their relatives who, they said, were travelling on the boats targeted in the past two days.
"The captain gathered us together to give us good news that our fishermen are coming back... they're alive, they're okay," Ginger Reyes, 35, the wife of the captain of one of the vessels, told AFP.
As they waited, dozens of people protested the disappearance of eight fishermen between January and March, which family members and the NGO Human Rights Watch blame on US military personnel.
"I don't know what to do anymore... I can't eat, I can't sleep, thinking about my son. I want them to return him to me," said María Cueva, weeping as she held a photograph of the 25-year-old.
Washington denies any involvement in the disappearance of the eight men.
'We're all afraid'
The airstrikes have instilled deep fear in Ecuadoran fishermen.
"We're all afraid something might happen to us," Fausto Soza told AFP, adding he had not gone out to sea for two months for fear of being targeted.
US President Donald Trump's administration has not provided definitive evidence that the vessels it has been targeting in the Pacific and the Caribbean are involved in drug trafficking.
But his campaign of strikes has the full support of Ecuador's right-wing President Daniel Noboa, who has gone to war against the gangs that have sown terror in the South American country.
Ecuador serves as a gateway to international markets for 70 per cent of the cocaine from neighbouring Colombia and Peru, the world's leading producers of the drug.
Interior Minister John Reimberg claimed that the vessels targeted by US forces were used by drug traffickers to ship cocaine to Mexico and the United States.
Noboa in March was among the first leaders to join the US leader's "Shield of the Americas", a Washington-led coalition to combat drug trafficking in the region.
In recent weeks, US special forces have been carrying out joint operations with Ecuador's military.

Title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill three
Article:
BEIRUT: Israeli strikes in southern and eastern Lebanon late on Friday killed at least three people and injured 23, the Lebanese Health Ministry said.
The ministry said in a statement that strikes hit five locations in the southern Tyr and Nabatieh regions and the Bekaa region in the east.
It updated an earlier toll given by Lebanese official media, which had reported two of the deaths in the south.
The strikes came despite a truce between Israel and the Iran-backed Hizbollah fighter group.
Lebanon's state-run National News Agency (NNA) reported the strike hit near the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge, which the Israeli army said it had captured, though Hizbollah did not confirm losing it.
Two young men were targeted while riding a motorcycle in the city of Nabatieh, NNA said, adding that rescuers transported their bodies to a local hospital.
Israel announced on Thursday it had taken control of the ridge. Defence Minister Israel Katz said the military would work to "prevent the enemy from re-establishing itself in the area".
Israel stepped up strikes in the Nabatieh region on Friday and also targeted the village of Rmadiyeh in the Tyre area, located more than 10 kilometres from the Israeli border.
The ministry said the third person was killed and 15 others hurt there, including two children, three women and six rescuers.
A rescue service source earlier told AFP that the strike in the village, which is sheltering people displaced from other southern areas, had hit a house.
Israel and Hizbollah have been trading fire since March, when the militant group dragged Lebanon into the wider Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Iran.
Israel responded with airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.
The conflict has calmed since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding and a framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon were agreed in June, but Beirut still reports Israeli strikes.
Imran Riza, the UN humanitarian coordinator for Lebanon, said on X on Friday that families returning to Nabatieh following the truce "face widespread destruction, lack of basic services, ongoing insecurity and uncertainty".

Title: Trump says envoys taking plan to 'end the war' to Moscow, Kyiv
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday that he was sending envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to Moscow and Kyiv with a plan to end the four-year-old Ukraine war.
It will be the first time that Trump's son-in-law Kushner and businessman friend Witkoff have visited war-torn Kyiv since Trump returned to office last year with a vow to solve the conflict.
Both US envoys have previously visited Moscow, leading to accusations that they have taken Russia's side in negotiations.
"They're bringing with them a proposal to end the war," Trump told reporters when asked about the trip.
Trump would not say whether the plan involved Ukraine ceding territory, as he has previously suggested, but added: "We have an idea for peace."
"I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They've done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we'll do it," he said.
The US leader blamed the war that began with Russia invading Ukraine in February 2022 on a "personality problem" between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Zelenskyy earlier said he had proposed observing a ceasefire with Russia while the US envoys visit Moscow and Kyiv.
"There will be no airstrikes on our part, and Russia must reciprocally ensure a ceasefire – without its own airstrikes – for the duration needed to conduct these talks," Zelenskyy said in his evening address.
A senior Ukrainian official told AFP the two envoys would visit Kyiv on Sunday. The Kremlin declined to comment on the matter.
A report in the US news outlet Axios said Kushner and Witkoff would travel on Friday, meet Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday, and then Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Sunday.
The two men have also been involved in negotiations for ceasefires in Gaza and Iran.
Trump meanwhile played down Germany's move earlier this week to blame Russia for an attempted drone attack on an airport.
"I speak to him. I know him very well. Putin's not looking to attack Nato territory," Trump said in the Oval Office when an AFP reporter asked him about the German allegation.
Trump has long been sceptical about maintaining support for Ukraine and had a televised row with Zelenskyy in the Oval Office in February 2025. With Putin, he has veered between friendliness and frustration.
The US leader said on Thursday that he would ask Europeans to repay the American aid provided to Ukraine under the administration of his predecessor Joe Biden.
Trump has long demanded that Europeans shoulder more of the cost of Western support for Ukraine.

Title: Massive fire breaks out at iconic Chew Jetty in Penang [WATCH]
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A massive fire broke out at Chew Jetty here this morning, with firefighters rushing to the scene to put out the blaze.
The number of structures affected was not immediately known.
Chew Jetty, one of George Town's best-known waterfront landmarks, is the largest and one of the oldest of Penang's Chinese clan jetties.
Built on wooden stilts above the sea, the settlement dates back to the 19th century and was founded by Chinese immigrants from Fujian province who shared the Chew surname.
The waterfront community remains known for its traditional stilt houses, wooden walkways and rich Chinese heritage.

Title: Massive late-night crash completely blocks NKVE northbound [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All northbound lanes of the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) near Shah Alam were blocked following a late-night accident, bringing traffic to a standstill shortly before midnight.
The accident occurred at Km8.4 on the northbound stretch from Setia Alam towards Shah Alam.
In an update at 11.27pm, PLUS Malaysia Bhd (PLUS) said all northbound lanes were blocked and advised motorists to exit at the Setia Alam toll plaza and use alternative routes.
At 12.04am, PLUS said the situation remained unchanged, with traffic still at a standstill. The right lane of the southbound carriageway was also obstructed.
"Northbound traffic is not moving. Use alternative routes and exit at the Setia Alam or Bukit Raja toll plazas," it said.
Photographs and video from the scene showed what appeared to be a large overhead highway gantry lying across the carriageway, with several heavy vehicles, including lorries, nearby.
Debris was scattered across the highway and central divider, while emergency vehicles were seen at the scene.
Photographs from the opposite carriageway showed a long queue of vehicles caught in the congestion.
The cause of the accident and whether there were any casualties were not immediately known.

Title: Serian haze emergency: DOE ramps up monitoring, enforcement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Environment (DOE) has raised air quality monitoring and preparedness to the highest level after a haze emergency was declared in Serian, Sarawak, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) hit 477  last night.
DOE deputy director‑general (development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said monitoring and field operations will be strengthened under the National Haze Action Plan (NHAP) and Nadma Directive No. 1 on disaster management.
She stressed that DOE's jurisdiction covers environmental quality monitoring, prevention and enforcement against open burning and pollution sources under environmental laws.
Disaster management, she said, will be carried out in an integrated manner with Nadma, the state government and relevant agencies according to their respective roles.
Besides Serian, three other areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API levels: Kuching (299), Samarahan (286) and Sri Aman (247). Another 18 areas nationwide also reported unhealthy readings.
Sarawak DOE has stepped up Open Burning Prevention Operation (OMPT) patrols at high‑risk sites including peatland, forests, landfills and agricultural areas.
"The DOE is closely monitoring peatland bush fires at Jalan Sibujaya Barat, covering 10 hectares, and Sungai Nai, Daro, covering three hectares, in Mukah. Drone flights will be conducted to obtain the latest overview," Azuri said.
The public is urged to report fire or open burning incidents immediately to the Fire and Rescue Department via 999 or DOE's toll‑free line 1‑800‑88‑2727.– BERNAMA

Title: 'Election stunt' jibes won't stop Ab Rauf from backing p-hailing riders
Article:
AYER KEROH: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh remains unfazed by claims that his recent ride-along with p-hailing workers was merely an "election stunt", saying his priority is to understand their challenges and find ways to help.
He said joining a delivery rider's routine gave him a closer insight into the fatigue, road risks and responsibilities faced by p-hailing workers supporting their families.
"Let them make whatever accusations or assumptions they want. Our job is not to answer every allegation, but to go to the ground, listen and find ways the government can help the people, including the p-hailing community," he said.
He was speaking at the launch of Karnival Anak Muda (KAM) Melaka during the Jom Heboh concert at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here last night.
Ab Rauf also announced RM300,000 in aid for riders attending the event, with each receiving RM100.
He said the state government's efforts to support p-hailing workers predated his ride-along last Wednesday, when he accepted and delivered a food order to experience their working conditions firsthand.
Among the initiatives are eight strategically located Rider Pitstops, providing rest facilities for riders.
"Through KAM, the state government is introducing three initiatives for Melaka's p-hailing community: motorcycle maintenance subsidies and discounts to reduce costs; a discounted workshop in every state constituency; and efforts to explore Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) coverage to strengthen their long-term safety and welfare," he said.
The three-day carnival features about 30 programmes covering motorsports and automotive activities, education and careers, technical and vocational education and training (TVET), sports, e-sports, entrepreneurship, recreation and entertainment.
Prizes include 20,000 T-shirts, 2,000 helmets, 38 motorcycles and a Yamaha RXZ as the grand prize.

Title: Judge declares mistrial in Lindsay Clancy child-killing case, puts ruling on hold for appeal
Article:
PLYMOUTH, United States: A judge declared a mistrial on Friday in the high-profile case of an American woman who killed her three children but put his decision on hold to allow the defence to appeal the decision.
Judge William Sullivan said he was freezing his mistrial ruling in the trial of Lindsay Clancy for one hour to allow her lawyer to file an appeal with a higher court.
The jury has been deadlocked 11-1 with the majority apparently leaning towards finding the 36-year-old Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity.
The dramatic developments came after the jury sent a note to the judge Friday morning saying that it was with a "heavy heart" that they were unable to reach a verdict in the case, which has cast a spotlight on maternal mental heath.
Clancy does not deny strangling Cora, five, Dawson, three, and Callan, eight months, but claims she was suffering from postpartum psychosis – excusing her from criminal responsibility.
To reach a verdict, all 12 jurors must be in agreement. If they cannot agree, the judge declares a mistrial and prosecutors must decide whether to try the case again with a new jury.
Kevin Reddington, Clancy's lawyer, has repeatedly demanded the replacement of the holdout juror with one of several alternate jurors but Sullivan declined to do so.
Clancy's televised five-week trial, which featured more than 80 witnesses and days of distressing testimony, has sparked debate in the United States over maternal mental health.
Clancy has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, saying she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children.
Her lawyers say this was caused by postpartum psychosis, a condition that experts say affects about one to two women in every 1,000 births.
Prosecutors have rejected that argument, saying Clancy had carefully planned the murders of her children and was able to understand the consequences of her actions.
Psychiatrists and people close to Clancy, as well as her estranged husband, were among the witnesses who testified about her fragile mental health during the trial.
- 'LOUSY MEDICAL CARE' -
Dozens of women dressed in pink have showed up at the court in Plymouth to extend their support for Clancy – and to make a statement about women's health more generally.
During closing arguments, Reddington, Clancy's lawyer, said she had made numerous pleas for help before the killings but had received "lousy medical care" from the doctors she consulted.
After the murders at the family home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, in January 2023, Clancy jumped from a second-story window in an apparent suicide attempt that left her paralysed from the waist down.
The former nurse faces life in prison without the possibility of parole if found guilty of first-degree murder.
Jurors can also find Clancy guilty of second-degree murder, manslaughter, or not guilty by lack of criminal responsibility – a verdict that would see her confined to a psychiatric facility.
The trial has revived memories of a similar case that also captivated the country 25 years ago, that of Andrea Yates, a Texas mother who drowned her five children in 2001.
Yates was initially convicted and sentenced to life in prison, but she was found not guilty by reason of insanity at a 2006 retrial and committed to a psychiatric hospital.--AFP

Title: Pas political cooperation subject to Syura Ulama Council review
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas says all political cooperation it undertakes is carefully scrutinised and reviewed before being referred to its Syura Ulama Council for guidance.
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the party's decisions were guided by the council.
"Rest assured, any political cooperation we enter into is not decided casually after a single meeting.
"We scrutinise and review every aspect before referring it to the Syura Ulama Council for guidance. That is why Pas has never lost out through its political cooperation," he said.
He was speaking at the Pas 75th anniversary grand ceramah here today, which was also attended by party president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang.
Tuan Ibrahim said Pas was confident its cooperation with strategic partners, including Barisan Nasional and Umno, would benefit all parties in efforts to take over the administration of Putrajaya.
He urged party members to place their full trust in the leadership and remain patient and steadfast.

Title: Pas won't sacrifice principles just to win, reach Putrajaya – Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas is attracting interest from various quarters, with several new parties keen to join forces and work with it, says its deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man.
He said Pas welcomed any party that wanted to work with it but would not sacrifice its principles for electoral victory.
"If all we wanted was to win and reach Putrajaya, it would not be difficult. We could simply join any party, regardless of whether it is right or wrong.
"But that is not our approach. We adhere to the principles set by Allah, including in political cooperation and alliances," he said.
Tuan Ibrahim was speaking at the Pas 75th anniversary grand ceramah here today, attended by party president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang.
He said Pas was preparing to take over the administration of the Federal Government, but added that party strength alone was insufficient.
"We must also examine our personal conduct and practices. Do not let our own actions become an obstacle to the victory of Islam.
"Leaders at all levels, in particular, must constantly reflect on their conduct," he said.

Title: Fadhlina urges parents, schools to follow official haze updates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has urged parents and school communities to monitor haze updates through official channels of the Sarawak State Education Department to ensure children's safety.
In a Facebook post tonight, she stressed that the health and safety of students must be prioritised, with the department continuing to monitor conditions closely.
"Take care of your health and reduce outdoor activities during this haze condition. The safety of the children and school community is our priority," she said.
Earlier, the department announced the temporary closure of 647 schools from Sept 7 to 11 due to unhealthy API readings. The closure involves 563 primary schools with 108,477 pupils and 84 secondary schools with 90,082 students, with Teaching and Learning at Home (PdPR) implemented.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to the proclamation of a haze emergency in Serian after pollution levels reached hazardous thresholds threatening public health.– BERNAMA
